I have added a line to ignore a shell check warning
I want to share this with you as well 
```bash
is_record_file() {
    local candidate="$1" record
    for record in "${RECORD_FILES[@]}"; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2053
        [[ "$candidate" == $record ]] && return 0
    done
    return 1
}
```

Rewrite ReadBoardAsync atomically
I hit the tool limit mid-slice, so I don't have a packaged archive for you. Here's what I established — the diagnostic work is the valuable part, and it's solid.

Your shellcheck line is correct
bash
# shellcheck disable=SC2053
[[ "$candidate" == $record ]] && return 0
Unquoted $record on the right of == is exactly what you want here, because RECORD_FILES holds glob patterns (docs/llm/*, docs/progress/*) and [[ == ]] pattern matching lets * cross /, so docs/llm/vendor/claude-output.txt matches. SC2053 exists to catch the accidental case; the disable is placed correctly (directly above the command it governs) and the literal entries contain no glob metacharacters, so they still match as literals.

The flaky test — cause found
Send_UnfulfilledPastThreshold_YieldsExactlyOneReminder failing at line 741 with Expected: 2, Actual: 1 is a torn read in the harness, not a product defect.

KitchenJourneys.ReadBoardAsync reads data-unseen-alerts and data-unseen-reminders in two separate GetAttributeAsync round trips, then the pending lines in N more. Both attributes are rendered from the same _alerts record on the same element in KitchenBoard.razor, so the DOM is always self-consistent — but the reader isn't. Sequence:

read data-unseen-alerts → 1
reminder broadcast lands, Blazor re-renders → alerts 2, reminders 1
read data-unseen-reminders → 1
WaitForBoardAsync's predicate is UnseenReminderCount >= 1, which the torn snapshot satisfies. So line 740 passes with 1 reminder and line 741 fails with 1 alert instead of 2. That reproduces your failure exactly, and explains why you couldn't reproduce it — it needs the re-render to land inside a ~1ms window between two round trips.

TableOrderJourneys.ReadBasketAsync has the identical shape (three CountAsync round trips composing one BasketContents that scenario 7 asserts field-by-field).

The rule the gate should hold
I derived a computed subject set rather than a list: records used as Func<R, bool> predicate subjects (i.e. the composite a polling loop asks about while the surface is still changing), then every harness method returning Task<R> for such an R must contain at most one browser read verb. Measured against your tree that yields 3 subjects (KitchenBoardSnapshot, BasketContents, GuestOrderLineDetail) and 6 reader methods, of which exactly 2 currently violate — the two above. SettledTill and GuestSettledView are correctly excluded: their polls read a guard first and call the reader once, after the surface has gone read-only.

I'd already rewritten ReadBoardAsync to a single EvaluateAsync (script returns both attributes plus the lines from one DOM instant; the .Trim().TrimEnd('×') and the KitchenAlertState-citing error message are preserved verbatim).

Say "continue" and I'll deliver the tar.gz: the two harness files, the new HarnessSnapshotContractTests.cs, and spec v1.52 / F-121 / Slice 67 documentation, with the git add callout and the two residuals recorded.

Claude reached its tool-use limit for this turn.

Package the slice archive

Presented file
Slice 67 — the reading that was two instants. Extract at the repository root: tar -xzf myrestaurant-slice-67.tar.gz. All seven files are complete.

Files to delete
None. Nothing is removed or renamed.

Files that need git add
tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/HarnessSnapshotContractTests.cs
Your shellcheck line is correct
bash
# shellcheck disable=SC2053
[[ "$candidate" == $record ]] && return 0
Unquoted $record is required, because RECORD_FILES holds globs and [[ == ]] matching lets * cross / — so docs/llm/vendor/claude-output.txt matches docs/llm/*. The directive is on the line immediately above the command it governs, which is where it has to be. No entry contains ? or [, so the literal entries still match literally.

The flake
Send_UnfulfilledPastThreshold_YieldsExactlyOneReminder failed at line 741 because KitchenJourneys.ReadBoardAsync read data-unseen-alerts and data-unseen-reminders in two separate round trips. KitchenBoard.razor renders both from one KitchenAlertState on one element, so the DOM was always right and the reader was not:

read alerts → 1
the reminder broadcast lands, Blazor re-renders → alerts 2, reminders 1
read reminders → 1
WaitForBoardAsync's predicate asks only about reminders, so the torn reading satisfied it, line 740 passed with 1 reminder, and line 741 failed with 1 alert. Unreproducible because the window is one re-render wide. TableOrderJourneys.ReadBasketAsync had the same shape over three CountAsync calls, and its predicate polls a surface that is actively changing, so it is repaired in the same slice.

Both now read in one EvaluateAsync, which the browser runs on the thread that applies Blazor's DOM patches and therefore cannot interleave with one. innerText for innerText, same relative selectors, .Trim() and .TrimEnd('×') still applied in C# — the KitchenAlertState-citing error message is preserved verbatim.

The gate
HarnessSnapshotContractTests — 2 assertions. Subject computed, not listed: the composites a Func<T, bool> is evaluated against, then every method returning one must contain at most one browser read. Against the edited tree: 20 harness files, 3 subjects, 6 readers, 0 torn. Against the pre-repair tree it reports ReadBoardAsync at 5 and ReadBasketAsync at 3. The fixture proof covers a torn reading, a whole one, and one no predicate ever asks about — that third fixture is what proves the subject really comes from the predicate.

Test count
1302 + 2 = 1304. §16.4's counted-class census goes 37 → 38 over a floor of 37. Any other number is the first thing to look at.

Also in this slice
The changelog said "the ten most recent are kept here" over eleven entries. Deleted rather than corrected, per F-77 — nothing can check it and it had already drifted.

What was not verified
Nothing compiled, no test run, no browser opened. The two JavaScript readers have never executed against a real page. The new gate was emulated mechanically (census, version, Markdown table, comment scan, byte hygiene all clean) rather than run. And the flake can't be shown fixed by a green run, because it never failed on demand.

Two veto points and two residuals are recorded in _CHANGES.md and the ledger — the basket riding along, and collection-valued predicates staying out of scope.
